# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–36 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of ninth year after Waterloo (1830). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter). Dinner for Emperor of China scheduled Monday, 8th July (three weeks ahead as of Chapter 35). Chapter 36 set in market towns (Bryngate, Mirecombe, Coldcombe, Dunholt) and London (Welbeck Street, Islington).
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Langham Hotel, Euston Square Railway Station, Bruton Street, Lincoln's Inn, Queen's Gate, Islington, Pall Mall East, Trafalgar Square); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, Coldcombe, Mirecombe, Gulton, Harrowgate, Beccles, Bryngate, Dunholt, Salwick).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review; praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Chapter 35 (late): Mr. Broune proposed marriage. Found he had human heart she could touch. Asked him to leave. Promised written answer by Thursday. By six o'clock evening: Sent rejection letter via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets. In debt; feared unpaid baker, son's horses, his dissipation. Lying became her nature. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Roger Carbury; returned home to find Paul and Henrietta together. Disbelieved Paul's accidental visit claim though Roger believed him. Cross-examined Henrietta on intentions regarding Paul. Expressed scorn at Henrietta's suggestion of marrying for railway fortune, despite her own efforts to secure advantageous matches for Felix. Allowed Henrietta to leave after kissing.

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Thursday evening: Kissed Marie's lips when alone. Chapter 35: Returned home nearly drunk. Made appointment with Ruby Ruggles at kitchen-garden bottom (Sheep's Acre); neglected it. Melmotte offered advancement and £200 cheque if Felix withdrew from Marie. Ashamed of treating Ruby badly; consoled himself that renunciation letter would not prevent running away with her if worth his while. Chapter 36: Wrote letter to Ruby excusing himself, claiming summoned to Liverpool on American railway business. Corresponding with Mr. Ramsbottom at Liverpool. Ramsbottom suggested Felix visit; his Board conduct resulted from Ramsbottom's advice, though Mrs. Hurtle dread strengthened invitation.

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Within week, Paul returned "as still dear friend," promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. When meeting Roger at door, showed "more graciousness." Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul Montague thoroughly in love with her. Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street in Lady Carbury's absence. When discovered together, Henrietta felt caught though innocent. Told mother: "He is so much above me, that, though I do love him, I cannot think of him in that way. And I have told you that I do love some one else." Praised Roger as "rock of strength" who "never lies. He never takes what is not his own." Kissed mother and left after her anger softened.

## Ruby Ruggles
Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre). Pretty with long glossy ringlets, large dark eyes, clear complexion. Felix preferred her to Marie. Made appointment at kitchen-garden; waited in vain. For three weeks heard nothing. Chapter 35: After John Crumb arrived with Joe Mixet for supper, received them with cool indifference. While men smoked, fled to yard. John made motion toward Ruby with right hand. Ruby escaped to bedside, afraid to undress. Subsequently took herself off from farm entirely. **Chapter 36: Now in London, working as servant/maid to Mrs. Hurtle at Islington. Recognized Paul Montague when he arrived seeking Mrs. Hurtle. Had seen Sir Felix more than once since arrival in London. Knew Roger Carbury was searching for her; learned this from Felix. Felt caught when Paul appeared, initially not remembering he'd asked for Mrs. Hurtle.**

**John Crumb**: Country lover from Suffolk. Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand. Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. Grandfather and Father Barham ordered waggonette to Beccles railway station when John arrived. Chapter 36: Had been communicating with Ruby and searching for her, avoiding Paul after initial encounter.

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. Chapter 35: Consulted Roger and Father Barham about Ruby's departure. Revealed Ruby "liked him well enough till she'd seed somebody else." Chapter 36: Has quarrelled with John Crumb; no longer anxious to get back granddaughter. Initial fright has passed; now reconciled to loss and saving of money.

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. Rumours of gigantic swindler. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Planning Emperor of China dinner (8th July). Chapter 35: Board meeting addressed directors; proposed adjournment one week. When Paul pressed for details, responded curtly. Beckoned Felix privately. Suggested adding directors from Longestaffe family. Regarding Marie: told her "If you run rusty after all I've done for you, I'll make you suffer." Offered Felix: renounce suit in writing, Melmotte will "stick to you and make a man of you" and give £200 cheque. Swore on honour: if Marie married Felix, she'd never have single shilling; would make will leaving all to St. George's Hospital. Chapter 36: Avoided Paul after Board meeting; took Felix with him into inner room.

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough. Chapter 35: Engaged to Lord Nidderdale. More than week since seeing Felix. Wrote begging to hear from him; entrusted letter to Didon. Father intends August wedding to Nidderdale. Marie declared: "It is no use, father, for I will never have him." Refused to give Felix up. Not wedded to Grosvenor Square grandeur; unafraid of starvation if married to Felix.

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made protest against Melmottes. Following morning received invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square. Chapter 35: Wrote to Lady Monogram (formerly Julia Triplex). Julia replied: husband forbids calling on Melmottes. Georgiana (unmarried twelve years) sobbed. Sir Damask led her out, put her in Madame Melmotte's carriage.

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. States father cannot sell Pickering without his consent.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles.

**Financial Strategy**: Stock at par; shares sold at premium "to run them up even to 110," yielding minimum three hundred thousand dollars. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Dislikes Fisker. Trembles for his money. Thoroughly in love with Hetta. Only Hetta serves as confidant. Chapter 35: Board meeting—pressed Melmotte for details; challenged him on shares and scrip. Chapter 36: Returned from Liverpool Friday morning. Felt must tell Mrs. Hurtle face-to-face he would not marry her due to dissatisfaction with her past. After Board, joined Nidderdale at Beargarden. Later visited Hetta at Welbeck Street; claimed visit accidental. **Walked with Roger to his hotel. Confided Mrs. Hurtle had come to London; he'd been with her three or four times. Told Roger all—rumoured duel, rumoured murder, rumour of existing husband. Declared: "But even if the rumours be untrue I will not marry her." Roger urged him to cheat "the Devil" if bargain made. Resolved Paul should go to Islington next morning, tell Mrs. Hurtle all stories heard, declare resolution never to marry her. Both felt certain she would show "claws" before story's end. Roger offered to visit her himself; Paul refused, feeling bound to incur risk himself. Saturday morning: Paul woke like "man condemned to die." Considered postponement to Monday. At last dressed quickly, worked himself into fortitude, took Hansom cab to Islington about 9 A.M.—found Mrs. Hurtle out for the day, returning tonight. Girl at door was Ruby Ruggles.**

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday (after Liverpool Tuesday). During earlier engagement promised to follow him; renewed promises in New York. Theatre evening: Paul took her; she noted woman in play whose lover talked to another, noting near-identical position to her own. After theatre, declined cab but Paul accompanied. Does not like Frenchmen; prefers Englishmen to Americans; thinks could never like English women. Hates "buckram" and forced propriety. Thinks he should marry her or world should hear story of his perjury. Believes he promised marriage. Chapter 36: Out for the day; returning tonight.

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie for fortune. Claims not afraid of Melmotte. Chapter 35: Marie engaged to Nidderdale. Chapter 36: At Beargarden with Paul. Questioned Paul regarding Melmotte's trustworthiness. Expressed concern about marrying for money if money doesn't exist.

## Mr. Broune
Editor, "Morning Breakfast Table." Nearer fifty than sixty; young of his age. Chapter 35 (late evening): Proposed to Lady Carbury. When he read her rejection letter: stood at fireplace, left letter on table. Woman wasn't in love with him! Yet he felt admiration greater than ever.

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Took Oxford degree; became "pervert," supposed "convert." Works as priest on day-labourer's wages. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall; consulted by Daniel Ruggles and Father Barham about Ruby. Ordered waggonette to Beccles. Chapter 36: Attended soirée with Lady Carbury. Found Paul and Henrietta together. Suspected circumstances though believed accidental visit explanation. Walked with Paul to his hotel. Confirmed John Crumb knew Ruby as "friends" in Suffolk and lied about it. Noted Crumb habitually lies but will eventually become perfect liar.

## Other Characters
- **Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour.
- **Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles. Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall with Ruggles and Roger.
- **Mr. Ramsbottom**: Liverpool gentleman. Suggested Paul visit; advised Felix's Board conduct. Paul corresponded with him regarding Mrs. Hurtle matter.
- **Rural Characters (Chapter 36)**: Market towns feature unnamed townsfolk. Elnelle Lindson mended torn sleeves, said little. Cotho Hollwood watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; later confided fire at Salford granary was set on purpose. Gamira Brackwood complained of aching back; walked long way round to avoid muddy square. Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage.
